data.text: Non-hand input techniques in virtual reality include head, eye, full-body, and sound-based tracking. Full-body tracking captures movement beyond the head, hands, and eyes to enhance self-embodiment and social presence, and can be implemented through motion capture suits or camera-based systems. Sound-based tracking captures voice and other sounds using microphones or microphone arrays for interaction.

Full-body tracking can be implemented through motion capture suits or camera-based systems.

data.text: The processing part of a VR system processes data from input sensors to activate output devices, with hardware selection depending on the application, users, and immersion level. The major components of the processing element are the GPU, CPU, and RAM. GPUs are useful for rendering complex graphics and speed up the rendering process due to their parallel processing abilities. GPU support is preferable for performance, multicore processors increase capacity, and at least 8 GB of RAM is typically preferable for XR engines.
points: The processing part of a VR system processes data from input sensors to activate output devices.
Hardware selection depends on the application, target users, available devices, and the required immersion level.
The major components of the VR processing element are the GPU, CPU, and RAM.
GPUs are useful for rendering complex graphics and speed up the rendering process due to their parallel processing abilities, and multi-GPU-enabled systems are typically used for VR applications.
Multicore processors increase computational capacity, but GPU support is preferable for performance, and at least 8 GB of RAM is typically preferable for XR engines.

data.text: Output devices for virtual reality include visual, audio, haptics, motion, and sensory outputs for taste and smell. Visual displays are categorized into head-mounted displays, world-fixed displays, and regular displays. Head-mounted displays are sophisticated wearable devices that more commonly provide stereoscopic viewing and come in non-see-through, optical see-through, and video see-through types. World-fixed displays are stationary surfaces, while regular displays are mobile devices mostly used for augmented reality.
points: VR output devices include visual, audio, haptics, motion, and sensory outputs for taste and smell.
Visual displays are categorized into head-mounted displays, world-fixed displays, and regular displays.
Head-mounted displays are sophisticated wearable devices that more commonly provide stereoscopic viewing.
Head-mounted displays can be non-see-through, optical see-through, or video see-through.
World-fixed displays are stationary surfaces, while regular displays are mobile devices mostly used for augmented reality.

data.text: Audio output provides specialized 3D audio, with headphones being preferred for a fully immersive system. Haptic devices provide touch sensations and are categorized as active versus passive, tactile versus proprioceptive, and self-grounded versus world-grounded. Motion platforms move the body to produce a sense of physical motion, and passive platforms are likely to result in less motion sickness. Treadmills provide the sense of walking or running in place and can be either active or passive.
